WITH observatory_telescope_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    observstation,
    COUNT(*) as telescope_count
  FROM telescopes
  GROUP BY observstation
),
total_telescopes AS (
  SELECT SUM(telescope_count) as total_count
  FROM observatory_telescope_counts
),
observatory_shares AS (
  SELECT 
    otc.observstation,
    otc.telescope_count,
    100.0 * otc.telescope_count / tt.total_count as share_pct
  FROM observatory_telescope_counts otc
  CROSS JOIN total_telescopes tt
),
average_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share_pct) as avg_share_pct
  FROM observatory_shares
),
above_average_observatories AS (
  SELECT 
    obs.observstation,
    obs.telescope_count,
    obs.share_pct,
    (obs.share_pct - avg_shr.avg_share_pct) as share_excess
  FROM observatory_shares obs
  CROSS JOIN average_share avg_shr
  WHERE obs.share_pct > avg_shr.avg_share_pct
)
SELECT 
  AVG(telescope_count) as avg_telescope_count,
  AVG(share_pct) as avg_share_pct,
  AVG(share_excess) as avg_share_excess
FROM above_average_observatories;

assumptions.assumption: "The average share" in the output refers to the average percentage of telescopes for observatories above the overall average (parallel structure to "the average telescope count"), not the overall average share itself. The third output (average excess) implicitly references the overall average share used for comparison.

alternatives.interpretation: "The average share" in the output refers to the overall average share across all observatories, not the average of the above-average observatories. This makes the three outputs: average telescope count for above-average observatories, the reference benchmark (overall average share), and how much above-average observatories exceed it.
